problem: Latent world models learn unconstrained future representations, so physical effects (dissipation, payload, actuation) stay entangled in transition weights, are not reusable, and give planners no physically meaningful quantity. Geometry-only neural time fields (ANTF) ignore how candidate motions actually execute under changing dynamics.
motivation: Collision-free geometric paths can become unsafe or slow when payload, ground response or actuation changes, and these effects show up only through interaction. Open-world navigation therefore needs an action-conditioned predictive model whose outputs a global planner can consume.
key_idea: Structure the latent world-model transition as a controlled dissipative port-Hamiltonian system (ELWM), and use its predicted candidate-wise terminal positions and traversal delays to rerank ANTF candidates via time-to-go = NTF(predicted terminal) + physical delay (PC-NTF).
insight: Imposing the pH structure (energy balance, nonnegative dissipation, control port) lowers motion prediction error and makes rollouts more action-dependent (action-intervention ratio 1.193 vs 1.009). Ablations show the physics must actually reach the planner: removing the physical condition or shuffling M_t degrades SPL and collisions (collision 18.75% and 22.11% vs 5.79%), and a generic WM gives similar quality but higher latency (479 vs 278 ms). Note the ablation table numbers differ from the main table.
method: Latent physical state encoder: encodes proprioceptive/interaction history (with robot meta-info) into slow physical regularity M_t, latent coordinates Q_t and velocities V_t; latent inertia G (Cholesky) gives momentum P=GV, so Z=[Q,P].
Latent stored energy: Hamiltonian H = kinetic (1/2 P^T G^-1 P) + potential U(rho(Q), M, mu_r), where rho uses relative features for translation invariance.

Port-Hamiltonian transition: dZ/dt=(J-R)∇H+B u with skew J, PSD dissipation R, control port B and latent control input; gives dH/dt = -∇H^T R ∇H + u^T y; rolled out with an implicit-midpoint discrete-gradient integrator.
Training: multi-step future-latent prediction loss against encodings of future histories, plus a SIGReg (LeJEPA) anti-collapse regularizer; energy residuals only logged for checkpoint selection.

Physics latent decoder: maps rollouts for each candidate command sequence to observable motion, terminal state, traversal delay and safety/tracking summaries, trained with Huber loss on physics-speed envelopes.

PC-NTF planning: ANTF supplies the nominal descent direction and shared candidates; ELWM predicts each one; the candidate cost is T(x_hat_{t+H}, g) + ΔT_phys, with penalties for poor tracking and speed violations, and the first action of the best candidate is executed. ELWM and NTF are frozen at evaluation.
Physics-conditioned Eikonal: generalizes S_geo to S_eff(x; zeta_t, mu_r) so that reduced capability increases the arrival-time gradient; velocity is projected by a deterministic safety layer.

setting.backbone: ELWM (port-Hamiltonian latent world model, trained from scratch) + Active Neural Time Fields (PINN, frozen) + physics latent decoder
setting.training_data: Interaction trajectories with RGB-D and inertial/proprioceptive histories in iGibson, HM3D-derived scenes and terrain-variation suite (carpet, tile, gravel, payload changes); NTF trained separately on scene geometry; size not stated
setting.observation: multimodal RGB-D + inertial/proprioceptive interaction history, executed actions, robot meta-info (mass/payload, limits)
setting.action_space: velocity commands (v, omega) with duration for a differential-drive robot; short-horizon candidate command sequences
setting.simulator: iGibson (including HM3D scenes converted to iGibson format)
setting.privileged: robot meta-information (mass/payload, velocity/acceleration limits) is given; goal supplied by upstream module from dataset

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out scenes/surfaces/robot meta-configs; exact size not stated
numbers.extra: Table 2 main comparison; ANTF baseline SR 81.3, SPL 0.64

numbers.eval_set_note: ablation setting; different numbers from main table
numbers.evidence: Table 'Ablation study of PC-NTF': ELWM + PC-NTF 1.012 / 0.661 / 5.79% / 278

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, no standard VLN/ObjNav benchmark. Intro says PC-NTF collision 12.1% vs Table 2's ANTF 14.4%, and energy residual 7.12e-7 vs 1.88e-7 in text: internal inconsistencies. Held-out regime/scene motion NRMSE 0.705/0.697 (Table 3) not listed as a separate row.
results: ELWM lowers 0.8 s motion NRMSE from 0.36 (capacity-matched Generic WM) to 0.29. PC-NTF improves over ANTF from SR 81.3 to 89.7, SPL 0.64 to 0.73, and Eikonal residual 0.083 to 0.031. It beats Generic WM+MPC in SR (87.1) and collisions (6.5%), roughly ties on SPL (0.74 vs 0.73), and has about half the latency (193 vs 372 ms), but is slower than ANTF (35 ms).
limitations: Only planar simulated navigation with an isotropic traversal-speed hypothesis; no real robot or broader robot configurations.
Custom benchmark and baselines (ANTF, one generic WM), with no comparison on standard navigation benchmarks; numbers are inconsistent across text, tables and ablation.
Extra latency over ANTF; gains over generic WM+MPC are mainly in Eikonal residual and latency, and SPL is not better.
